checked_sources: Galloni, Laffere & Rancz 2020 eLife 9:e55761 — full text (Europe PMC PMC7334021)
evidence_location: Results, text accompanying Fig. 2C (apical trunk lengths); Results text on the shortened Hay-model morphology (Ca2+ hot zone); Fig. 3A legend (recording site at main bifurcation)
quote: V1 mean = 409 ± 64 µm ... V2m mean = 313 ± 65 µm ... 685–885 µm in the long morphology
discrepancy: 313 and 409 µm are the V2m and V1 group MEANS (SD ~65 µm each), not a range of trunk lengths. The 685–885 µm figure is the position of the high-density Ca2+ 'hot zone' in the long (Hay et al. 2011) model, not the soma-to-bifurcation length; the Fig. 3A legend places that model's main bifurcation at 620 µm from the soma (vs 370 µm for the V2m cell). The paper does not itself describe the Hay model as 'rat-derived' (true of Hay 2011, but not stated here). The 500 µm slider default does lie within 313–885 µm either way.
suggested_fix: Mean apical trunk length (soma to main bifurcation) is 409 ± 64 µm in mouse V1 and 313 ± 65 µm in V2m (Galloni et al. 2020); in the Hay et al. (2011) thick-tufted model used by the same study the main bifurcation lies ~620 µm from the soma, with the dendritic Ca2+ hot zone at 685–885 µm.
bibliographic_issues: None; authors, year, journal, volume, article number and DOI match Europe PMC (PMID 32463356).

checked_sources: Chi, Jung & Cauwenberghs 2010 IEEE Rev Biomed Eng 3:106–119 — full text PDF (isn.ucsd.edu/pub/papers/rbme10.pdf)
Metting van Rijn et al. 1990 Part 1 — full text (biosemi.com author copy)
evidence_location: Chi: Sec. II.C 'Motion and Friction', p. 111 (triboelectric statement; eqs. 7–10); Sec. on noncontact electrodes, p. 114 and Fig. 7 caption (settling/recovery). Metting van Rijn: Sec. 2.3 (cable interference currents)
quote: No satisfying quantitative models exist to generally describe this effect ... Recovery times of upwards of 10 s
discrepancy: (1) Chi's 'no satisfying quantitative models' sentence refers specifically to triboelectric charge induced by lateral friction; the same section does give first-order quantitative treatment of transversal motion (coupling-impedance changes, balancing conditions eqs. 7–9) and a first-order triboelectric current term (eq. 10), so 'no model for motion and friction artefacts' overstates it. (2) Recovery: paper says 'upwards of 10 s' in text and 'more than 15 s' in Fig. 7, for a noncontact ECG sensor with 0.05 Hz high-pass after a lead disruption at t = 5 s; '10–15 s' is a reasonable gloss. (3) The 200 µV figure is from Metting van Rijn, not Chi: 10 nA p-p cable current, 20 kΩ mean electrode impedance, and 50% relative differences in BOTH interference current and electrode impedance give 200 µV p-p (the claim's single '50% mismatch' hides that both terms contribute).
suggested_fix: No satisfying quantitative model exists for the triboelectric charge generated by friction at the electrode–skin interface (transversal motion is modelled to first order as coupling-impedance change); capacitive non-contact electrodes can need more than 10–15 s to recover after a motion-induced overload; mains current coupled into cables (10 nA p-p, 20 kΩ electrodes, 50% differences in current and impedance) gives ~200 µV p-p of interference (Metting van Rijn et al. 1990).
bibliographic_issues: None; Chi journal header confirms IEEE Reviews in Biomedical Engineering vol. 3, 2010, pp. 106–119.

checked_sources: Iivanainen et al. 2021 NeuroImage 245:118747 — published full text (Europe PMC PMC8752968)
evidence_location: Published: Sec. 3.3 Results ('88, 35 and 26 eigencomponents'), Sec. 3.4.1 Results (400 samples / 60–70–80%; 80–30–20 samples for 90%), Sec. 3.4.2 Results (ROI: TI in bits and max SNR only). Preprint v1: p. 11 ('88, 35 and 25'; 'at maximum 179, 61 and 62'), p. 13 (400 samples / 60, 74, 80%), p. 14 ('Nine and eight components had SNR > 1')
quote: To explain 99% of the total variance, 88, 35 and 26 eigencomponents are needed
discrepancy: Every number in the claim matches the 2019 arXiv v1 preprint, but the cited published NeuroImage version differs: 26 (not 25) EEG eigencomponents for 99% variance; the 'maximum 62' and the '8 EEG components with SNR > 1' statements are not in the published text (ROI results are reported as total information in bits and max SNR). In the preprint the '8 components' figure applies to the SMALLER motor-cortex ROI with white sensor noise only; with coloured (brain-background) noise it drops to 4. Preprint high-noise figures are 60/74/80% (published: 60/70/80%); the EEG 80% and the 20-samples-for-90% values agree in both.
suggested_fix: Either cite the preprint explicitly for the 25 / 62 / 8-component figures, or update to the published values: 26 EEG eigencomponents (88 on-scalp MEG) for 99% variance; ~20 EEG samples for 90% of variance at high SNR, only ~80% with 400 samples at low SNR; and drop or qualify the '8 components with SNR > 1' (preprint, small ROI, white noise; 4 with brain-background noise).
bibliographic_issues: Published record matches Europe PMC (PMID 34852277). The arXiv preprint 1912.05401 (v1 only) carries a different title: 'Sampling theory for spatial field sensing: Application to electro- and magnetoencephalography'.
